results.draft_locus: How to Read This Register ¶1 and the entries R9/R15, R84/R106, R150/R159
results.quote: Where chapters cited the same legal text or page under two URLs, the single entry keeps both URLs.
results.finding: Both readers stopped at the deduplication rule because the register keeps several same-document pairs as separate entries (R9/R15 'The same report as R15, on another host', R84/R106, R150/R159; Reader A adds R227/R239, Reader B R13/R58), and the page never says when a duplicate is merged and when kept as two entries.

results.draft_locus: How to Read This Register ¶1 and entries R390, R97, R21
results.finding: Both readers met a contradiction: entries such as R390 '(page redirected; not read)' and R97 'known through search summaries only; the originals were not accessible' are listed under an R that is defined as a consulted source.

results.quote: Platform, data, ML and experimentation precedes Web, SEO and reliability, the reverse of their chapters, because the topic list the identifiers were assigned from put them in that order
results.finding: Both readers found the reason for the Platform/Web position circular (the order is explained by the order) and could not place the two sections. The spec's p06 prescribes both the reversed order and this reason, so the difficulty comes from the declared order, not from the prose.

results.draft_locus: Company sources: Adevinta and Schibsted, entries R74 and R75
results.quote: Kijiji impairment. *News and trade press.* Cited in: [[case-ebay-classifieds]].
results.finding: Both readers flagged R74 (eBay's 8-K on the eBay-Adevinta deal) and R75 (Kijiji impairment), cited only in case-ebay-classifieds, filed under Adevinta although the Topic Index says a source 'sits under the topic it serves best'. Reader A also lists R53 under Adevinta and R135/R160-R162 (Adevinta's own releases) under eBay Classifieds; Reader B reports only R74/R75.

results.draft_locus: Company sources: other marketplaces, entry R321
results.quote: in *The Site Reliability Workbook*, O'Reilly, 2018. SLIs as good-event ratios, SLOs, error budgets, critical user journeys. *Book.* Cited in: [[reliability-and-scale]].
results.finding: Both readers found a generic Google SRE book chapter filed under 'Company sources: other marketplaces' while its sibling R563 sits under Web, SEO and reliability; it reads as misfiled.

results.quote: The research briefs mentioned in the opening are left out: the chapters rely on these briefs, written in October 2026 to collect and check the company, regulatory and practice facts the chapters use.
results.finding: Both readers re-read this sentence: after the colon they expected the reason the briefs are left out and got a description of them, with the reason only in the next sentence; both also note the boundary blurs because the exception R566 is a 'digest in this book's research notes' (Reader B) or contradicts the opening's flat 'Only public sources are listed' (Reader A).

results.draft_locus: Regulation and standards R475-R478; also R37/R38, R181/R182, R317/R318, R352/R353
results.quote: Storage limitation and accountability; response deadline; erasure and its exceptions; notification of recipients.
results.finding: Both readers could not tell what each source supports where different documents share a word-for-word identical 'what it supports' clause (R475-R478 four times; R37/R38, R181/R182, R317/R318, R352/R353 named by both), and thought they were rereading the same entry.

results.quote: on which Valuo, the valuation model of Hearthly (the fictional Veldmark group's property portal), is described as trained.
results.finding: Both readers were jarred by the first appearance of Valuo and Hearthly, products of the fictional Veldmark, inside a regulation entry right after the Key Points say no source describes Veldmark; both re-read to check the source was not being claimed for the fiction (Reader B also notes the entry breaks the entry format with a dash).

results.quote: deduplicated by normalized URL: two links count as one source when they differ only in scheme, `www.`, a trailing slash, a fragment, an `.html` suffix or an arXiv version.
results.finding: Reader A met deduplication mechanics before the anatomy of an entry (¶3) and went back after reading ¶3; it suggests putting the entry anatomy first. The order p03-p04-p05 is the spec's declared order, so the fault is the spec. Reader B did not report this.

results.draft_locus: Company sources: AVIV and property portals, entry R205
results.quote: "Shipping the first MCP in HeyImmo" (January) and "What we learned from launching ImmoScout24 app in ChatGPT" (March).
results.finding: Reader A could not tell whether R205 is a separate source or a duplicate of R199 and R200 listed a few lines earlier. Reader B did not report this.

results.draft_locus: Company sources: OLX and Prosus, entry R82
results.quote: Prosus's FY25 results booklet (2025) records its de-prioritization in Europe.
results.finding: Reader A paused because a second source (R84/R106) is described inside R82's entry without its identifier. Reader B did not report this.

results.quote: The toolkit presents each template as the smallest form that makes a decision explicit, assigns an owner and leaves evidence someone else can check.
results.finding: Reader A read this as a detour in the middle of the chain and re-read to connect it to 'This chain is how that check is made'. Reader B did not report this.

results.draft_locus: All topic sections (e.g. Regulation and standards, R442 vs R489)
results.quote: The order was fixed when the identifiers were assigned and does not change.
results.finding: Reader B found the order of entries within each topic section unexplained (not alphabetical, not by year; apparently by first citing chapter), so it looked random. Reader A did not report this.

results.draft_locus: Trust, safety and fraud R401; Platform, data, ML and experimentation R508
results.finding: Reader B went back to check for a missed duplicate because R401 and R508 carry identical titles in different sections. Reader A did not report this.

results.draft_locus: Company sources: Adevinta and Schibsted, entry R31
results.finding: Reader B could not resolve what is superseded and by what. Reader A did not report this.

results.draft_locus: Entries R490, R97 and others using a dash before the supports clause
results.quote: — Debezium documentation, n.d. — keying events by aggregate ID to preserve per-aggregate order.
results.finding: Reader B re-parsed entries that put a dash instead of a period before the 'what it supports' clause; in R97 the dash clause reads as the supports clause. Reader A did not report the format breaks (only R410's content).

The does_not_know terms (liquidity, network effects, multi-homing, learning to rank, percolation, DAC7, P2B, statements of reasons, VINs, RESO/OpenImmo) appear only as subjects of listed sources in a register, and How to Read ¶2 points to [[glossary]] for plain-language definitions; non-obvious names are glossed (Aurelia UK Feederco Ltd, Productscape, Veldmark, Valuo/Hearthly). Neither flow reader reported an unexplained term.
Opens with the declared direct statement and moves at once to the research date, secondary summaries and names; no placeholder, restated question, dictionary or book-report opening.

Does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new subtopic or body evidence; the last paragraph restates Key Point 3 but follows a synthesis and a recommendation, so the conclusion does not end on a rephrased thesis alone.
States the toolkit-glossary-register chain no single section states, and says why it matters: a decision record can be traced to evidence of known kind and age; ¶2 gives the course of action.
¶1 returns to the toolkit's claim of evidence 'someone else can check'; ¶3 returns to Key Point 3 (Veldmark fictional, inferences and recommendations the author's judgement).

The cold reader predicted the section order (How to Read, Topic Index, thirteen topic sections, Sources by Chapter, closing link to toolkit and glossary), that only cited sources are listed once with year, type and citing pages, findable by topic or chapter, the October 2026 research, secondary summaries and 2026 names, that research briefs and Veldmark are not sources, and to weigh claims by kind and age; all of the expected answer.

The cold reader found R134 through the eBay Classifieds, Kleinanzeigen and Marktplaats topic section and via Sources by Chapter, and judged it a record of what the company said it built in 2019, past the three-year line, not a description of today, citing the evidence-type table; matches the expected answer.
